verdict_basis: Fresh valid generic-creole cases show that the Rust path does not preserve a literal backslash-n in href while normalizing only the title. Additional direct-anchor cases expose renderer divergence before link metadata can be compared. Any failing counterexample rejects the claimed invariant.

inputs.finding: Java and Rust both preserve the literal backslash-n in href and emit an XML newline in title.
Explicit tooltip is normalized independently of href and the visible label.
Invalid marker remains literal, the second implicit URL normalizes its title, and both links remain separate.
Rust matches Java's UTF-16 char-cast result, including the non-scalar U+F600 result for <U+1F600>.

axes: literal backslash-n in URL and tooltip
inputs.finding: Relevant counterexample: Java href is https://example.com/sequence/implicit\npath and title is the same URL with an actual newline; Rust emits href and title for only https://example.com/sequence/implicit and renders the remaining path as ordinary text. The generic sequence link path therefore violates both target preservation and title-only normalization. The note's explicit tooltip does pass, showing the failure is exercised by the literal backslash-n URL path.

Relevant counterexample: Java preserves https://example.com/class/implicit\npath in href and normalizes only its title; Rust truncates the parsed URL at the backslash-n and uses the truncated URL in href/title, with the suffix rendered outside the link. The explicit and invalid-marker anchors individually match, but the held-out implicit URL violates the stated invariant.

Secondary failure: the valid Java output contains a linked Service entity, while Rust emits no anchor and changes entity ordering/geometry. This is not an isolated normalization comparison because the state direct-anchor renderer diverges earlier, but it disproves the unqualified every-hyperlink claim and identifies the verbatim state.rs anchor surface for follow-up.

Secondary failure: valid Java DESCRIPTION output contains a linked component, while Rust selects a divergent cluster rendering and emits no anchor. This is a renderer-model failure before title normalization can be isolated, but it remains a failing fresh pair.

findings.claim_disproved: The generic creole path preserves every parsed target byte sequence in href while normalizing only title fields.
findings.evidence: In both families Java preserves the literal backslash-n as part of href and converts it only in title; Rust truncates the target and renders the suffix as ordinary text.

findings.claim_disproved: Every SVG hyperlink is covered by the shared normalization invariant.
findings.evidence: Both valid oracle outputs contain anchors that are absent from the Rust outputs due to preceding diagram-rendering divergence; the inspected state.rs and SvgBuilder direct-anchor paths also bypass the shared normalizer.

findings.claim_disproved: The supplied comparator artifact was used exactly as prescribed.
findings.evidence: The path exists but hashes to 807deb…, not the requested 20bf…. The requested digest was not found locally, and no cargo/rustc rebuild was permitted.

residue: The mixed sequence and class failures combine URL parsing/rendering with title normalization; they are still decisive because href preservation is part of the claimed invariant.
The state and component direct-anchor failures cannot isolate title bytes because those renderers diverge before anchor emission; they remain preserved as executable counterexamples.
